research_scope: Complete source-free first-pass scans and contextual links for 12 previously inventoried mathematical formulations; no new definitions or external research.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the pushout universal property of the cospan of arrows B→A and B→C and retained span/cocone and universal factorization references without assuming all categories are small.

references.context: Category theory: general possibly large category with objects and morphisms
references.reason: The only indexed general category meaning is explicitly small; avoid imposing unwarranted smallness.

references.phrase: morphisms B to A and B to C
references.context: Category theory: diagram of two arrows with a common source object
references.reason: The categorical span shape and its arrow family require contextual matching.

references.phrase: morphisms A to P and C to P agreeing on B
references.context: Category theory: cocone under a span B→A and B→C
references.reason: Compatible arrows defining the pushout cocone are not yet linked to an independent cocone meaning.

references.phrase: every other compatible pair factors uniquely
references.context: Category theory: universal property of a colimit cocone of span shape
references.reason: Uniqueness of the induced arrow is the universal-property clause.

references.disposition: P is the defined output object; it is not itself an additional missing contextual meaning.

items.review_rationale: Read Galois extension through algebraic, separable and normal extension meanings and base-preserving automorphisms, leaving finite degree [E:F] for global classification.

references.matching_note: The ambient extension is a general inclusion of fields.
Algebraicity is the corresponding extension-field property.
The Galois extension must be separable in the field-theoretic sense.
Normality is the existing normal algebraic extension property.
Automorphisms fixing the base field are independently indexed.

references.context: Field theory: degree of a finite field extension as vector space dimension over the base field
references.reason: The degree of an extension should be compared with the corpus's finite-extension/field-degree meanings.

references.disposition: Equality of two finite cardinal counts is a property, not a separate prerequisite.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed base-fixed automorphisms and the group law for the Galois group, linking the existing Galois extension, automorphism and abstract group contexts.

references.matching_note: The group is formed from an existing Galois field extension.
Composition of automorphisms yields an abstract group.

references.phrase: field automorphisms of E that fix F
references.matching_note: This is the precise base-preserving automorphism group of the extension.

references.disposition: Composition is the standard operation on maps, already implicit in the group of automorphisms.

items.review_rationale: Examined quasi-compactness of a continuous map through quasi-compact inverse-image subspaces and ordinary continuity, retaining inverse-image terminology for subsequent consolidation.

references.matching_note: The map is continuous between topological spaces.
The open subset has the finite-subcover compactness property.
The inverse-image subspace is quasi-compact.
An open subset is an ordinary subset of Y.

references.context: Set theory/topology: inverse image f^{-1}(U) of a subset under a map
references.reason: The inverse-image construction merits a shared candidate check during global consolidation.

items.review_rationale: Read quasi-compact topological space without a Hausdorff restriction and matched the no-Hausdorff finite-open-subcover formulation of compactness.

references.matching_note: X has an ordinary open-set topology.
The no-Hausdorff compactness definition uses finite open subcovers.

references.phrase: finite subcollection that still covers X
references.disposition: This is the defining finite-subcover condition, rather than an independent missing contextual meaning.
The clause explicitly denies a separation assumption and should not be construed as a separate dependency on Hausdorff spaces.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed degree-zero graded localization as a degree-graded subring of ordinary ring localization and stored graded-ring and homogeneous-element references for later classification.

references.matching_note: S_f is localization at powers of f.

references.context: Graded commutative algebra: positively graded ring with decomposition S=⊕ S_n
references.reason: Grading structure should not be conflated with a Noetherian graded-ring meaning.

references.context: Graded algebra: element belonging to one graded component S_d
references.reason: Homogeneity of ring elements is a specific graded context.

references.context: Graded algebra: homogeneous degree-zero component of a graded localization
references.reason: The S_(f) component is a ring construction and cannot be reduced to mere ordinary localization.

references.disposition: The displayed fraction-degree condition explicitly describes what belongs to the constructed subring.

items.review_rationale: Read the entire homogeneous ideal condition, relating ring ideals and S-submodules while separately recording graded rings and homogeneous components.

references.matching_note: A homogeneous ideal is first an ordinary ring ideal.
An ideal is an S-submodule of the ring regarded as its own module.

references.context: Graded algebra: ring with direct-sum decomposition and compatible multiplication
references.reason: The graded ring concept is not identical to the indexed Noetherian graded-ring context.

references.context: Graded algebra: degree-d homogeneous component of an element of a graded ring
references.reason: Componentwise membership criterion is a distinct graded-algebra construction.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed Proj(S) via spectrum, homogeneous ideals and arbitrary subspace topology, recording the graded ring and irrelevant ideal without presuming they already exist.

references.matching_note: Proj(S) is equipped with a topology.
The homogeneous prime ideals are primes of a commutative ring.
Proj(S) may be empty; use the general arbitrary-subspace version.
The underlying spectrum is the prime spectrum of the graded commutative ring.
This supplies the homogeneous condition for prime ideals.

references.context: Graded algebra: nonnegatively graded commutative ring S=⊕_{n≥0}S_n
references.reason: Ordinary Noetherian graded-ring context should not be assumed.

references.context: Graded algebra: ideal of positive-degree elements ⊕_{n>0} S_n
references.reason: The special ideal excluded from Proj is a contextual ring construction.

items.review_rationale: Read the standard étale polynomial quotient/localization criterion, distinguishing source ring homomorphism and étaleness from monic polynomial and formal derivative concepts.

references.matching_note: The étale ring-map definition uses the commutative unital algebra convention.
Standard étale is a particular presentation guaranteeing the existing étale property.
The quotient is taken after ring localization at polynomial g.

references.context: Commutative algebra: a standard étale algebra presentation by polynomial localization and quotient
references.reason: The compound quotient construction is not equivalent to any one existing ring-localization meaning.

references.context: Polynomial algebra: monic polynomial with leading coefficient 1 in R[x]
references.reason: This may be a separate indexed polynomial property; leave the occurrence unassigned.

references.context: Polynomial algebra: formal derivative of f and invertibility of its image after localization
references.reason: Differentiation of a formal polynomial differs from analysis derivative and must be context-matched.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed combinatorial equivalence of arrow families by their indexed targets and arrow occurrences, preserving reindexing without presuming an arbitrary category is small.

references.context: Category theory: indexed family of arrows in a category with common target U
references.reason: Potentially matches the existing fixed-target family meaning subject to categorical size context.

references.matching_note: The families are indexed by underlying sets; exact indexing-map structure recorded separately.

references.phrase: each family admits an indexing map into the other identifying the arrows
references.context: Category theory: reindexing of parallel arrow families by functions of index sets
references.reason: Combinatorial equivalence here ignores multiplicity and preserves the arrows.

references.disposition: Equality of the sets of occurrences of arrows, ignoring repeat indices, is specified directly by the formulation.

items.review_rationale: Examined covering-family axioms of a Grothendieck site and linked fixed-target arrow families, while leaving site, refinement and pullback context for later global comparison.

references.context: Category theory: category with a Grothendieck topology / specified covering families
references.reason: The Grothendieck site notion is not established by a generic category definition.

references.matching_note: An indexed family of morphisms has common target U.

references.context: Grothendieck sites: covering family containing an isomorphism to the target
references.reason: This is a covering-family closure axiom specialized to site structure.

references.context: Grothendieck sites: pullback/refinement of covering families along arbitrary arrows
references.reason: The site axioms invoke categorical pullback and compositional refinement, not generic set intersection.

items.review_rationale: Read geometrically normal algebra via scalar extension over any field and the existing normal ring property, while preserving k-algebra terminology for later consolidation.

references.matching_note: k is the base field.
A field extension may be arbitrary, not algebraic.
Extension of scalars of the k-algebra A to K is a base-change construction.
Normality is the existing commutative ring notion.

references.context: Commutative algebra: unital algebra over field k
references.reason: The algebra structure includes a scalar-structure homomorphism k→A; record as a candidate distinct from general ring maps.
